subtitle: The words of a study, from idea to result, and writing a summary
words.intro: At a German university the lecture hall is free, the professor is a civil servant and the student may stay for years. The one thing nobody escapes is the written summary.

grammar[0].fact: At German universities a doctorate often comes with a *Rigorosum* or *Disputation*, an oral defence, and the title *Dr.* may be printed on your ID card. Some people expect you to use it for life.

grammar[1].blocks[0].title: Four moves
grammar[1].blocks[1].root.yes.answer: Konjunktiv I or a source phrase
grammar[1].blocks[1].root.no.answer: your own view — leave it out
grammar[1].blocks[1].root.no.example: It belongs in a different text.
grammar[1].blocks[2].title: Nominalise to tighten, not to impress
grammar[1].blocks[2].text: *Nach Einführung der Regelung ging die Zahl der Unfälle zurück* — good. Three genitives in a row — turn one back into a verb.
grammar[1].blocks[3].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[1].fact: A summary in German must not sound as if you agree. So it runs on the Konjunktiv I and on verbs of saying: *Der Autor betont, kritisiert, räumt ein*. Each one tells the reader what you think of him without saying so.

document.intro: A real doctoral certificate from the year the physicist Friedrich Hund took his degree. One sentence fills most of the page. Look for the people, the subject and the two marks: this is noun style in its Sunday suit.
document.fact: Friedrich Hund went on to give his name to *Hund’s rules* in physics, and he lived to 101. The dean who signed this, Ludwig Prandtl, founded modern aerodynamics. Göttingen in those years could fill a page with signatures like these.

reading.intro: Maya is writing her first seminar paper at a German university, on neighbourhood gossip. She has a source of unusual quality. In the professor’s office, Prof. Dr. Lindner is reading it, with a pencil, and has stopped at footnote 14.
reading.photos[0].caption: Ein Hörsaal: Vorne die These, hinten das Handy.
reading.fact: German is unusually strict about citing. Politicians have lost their doctorates and their ministries over footnotes: *Plagiatsaffäre* is a word in every newspaper’s archive, and volunteers go through old theses line by line, on a public wiki.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Distance yourself from each claim, as a paper would.
